pr_title: Rewrite mania selection blueprint to use only `HitObject` (no `DrawableHitObject`) for layout
pr_body:
- Fixes #13297
- [x] Depends on #13498

The selection blueprint test scene is rewritten.
I couldn't come up with a test reproducing the crash, because it is depending on one-frame window of column movement and snapping. The chance of regression should be low if `DrawableHitObject` is going to be eliminated from selection blueprint.

Also, It was not necessary to this PR, but  I removed the lifetime override logic of `DrawableManiaHitObject`. It was unnecessary (and conflicting) because DrawableHitObject now has its own logic for that.

issue_context.title: Crash when hold note is moved between columns in mania editor
issue_context.body:
Probably known to @smoogipoo but I post here anyway.
Regressed in #12784.

```
System.InvalidOperationException: Cannot call InternalChild unless there's exactly one Drawable in Children (currently 0)!
   at osu.Framework.Graphics.Containers.Container`1.get_Child()
   at osu.Game.Rulesets.Mania.Objects.Drawables.DrawableHoldNote.get_Head() in /data/Projects/Osu/osu/osu.Game.Rulesets.Mania/Objects/Drawables/DrawableHoldNote.cs:line 31
   at osu.Game.Rulesets.Mania.Edit.Blueprints.HoldNoteSelectionBlueprint.get_ScreenSpaceSelectionPoint() in /data/Projects/Osu/osu/osu.Game.Rulesets.Mania/Edit/Blueprints/HoldNoteSelectionBlueprint.cs:line 76
   at osu.Game.Screens.Edit.Compose.Components.BlueprintContainer`1.ApplySnapResult(SelectionBlueprint`1[] blueprints, SnapResult result) in /data/Projects/Osu/osu/osu.Game/Screens/Edit/Compose/Components/BlueprintContainer.cs:line 502
   at osu.Game.Screens.Edit.Compose.Components.EditorBlueprintContainer.ApplySnapResult(SelectionBlueprint`1[] blueprints, SnapResult result) in /data/Projects/Osu/osu/osu.Game/Screens/Edit/Compose/Components/EditorBlueprintContainer.cs:line 71
   at osu.Game.Screens.Edit.Compose.Components.BlueprintContainer`1.moveCurrentSelection(DragEvent e) in /data/Projects/Osu/osu/osu.Game/Screens/Edit/Compose/Components/BlueprintContainer.cs:line 498
   at osu.Game.Screens.Edit.Compose.Components.BlueprintContainer`1.OnDrag(DragEvent e) in /data/Projects/Osu/osu/osu.Game/Screens/Edit/Compose/Components/BlueprintContainer.cs:line 189

```
comments: @smoogipoo you going to look into this one or shall i?

I've briefly looked into it but I'm not immediately sure how to fix the issue, so I'm not going to continue for now.

tl;dr: Move selection -> Defaults applied -> OnApply() -> free() -> clears nested hitobjects.

Regressed in https://github.com/ppy/osu/pull/12916 as a result of calling Beatmap.Update() on start time changes.

When a selected note is moved between columns, the hit object is removed from the playfield:

https://github.com/ppy/osu/blob/b5afe4e50608d8f8a2144ce599e71246f2f1145a/osu.Game.Rulesets.Mania/Edit/ManiaSelectionHandler.cs#L61-L63

And DHO will be removed:

<https://github.com/ppy/osu/blob/ff0494229524c7c5d984895f8500c31b8329185e/osu.Game/Rulesets/UI/HitObjectContainer.cs#L152-L156>

The removal of DHO from the `HitObejctContainer` immediately makes the DHO to be returned to the pool. The DHO nested hit objects are cleared:

https://github.com/ppy/osu/blob/40949f6c1b0c1088f4c28b94b8f9c30084952f69/osu.Game/Rulesets/Objects/Pooling/PoolableDrawableWithLifetime.cs#L91-L98

The `HitObjectUsageFinished` event above is supposed to remove corresponding blueprints. However, the blueprint removal is queued to the `HitObjectUsageEventBuffer`.
Thus, during the frame, the selection blueprint has a stale reference to the DHO.
The crash is due to the usage of this stale DHO.

Because `HitObjectUsageEventBuffer` is just introduced to this delayed blueprint removal, the remaining way to eliminate the stale DHO is to delay the returning of the DHO to the pool, somehow.
In the context of mania I don't think that's bad, but is that really what we want to do? From the context of arbitrary rulesets I mean...

That's a fair call. I only thought of exploring this direction upon seeing this comment:

https://github.com/ppy/osu/blob/3cd7d45b0fa3c15d7ceac2deb2cd94e469b41bb6/osu.Game.Rulesets.Mania/Edit/Blueprints/HoldNoteSelectionBlueprint.cs#L61

which made me think that referencing DHOs from blueprints was unwanted. May have misunderstood intent (that the `.IsLoaded` part is the problem).

I still think that is a good direction - the osu! blueprints were changed to refer to the `HitObject` in their `Update()` but unfortunately still use the DHO for these properties too... I would eventually like to see `DrawableObject` removed from the blueprints.

My concern here is around the overhead for something that's required for every ruleset with multiple playfields. Maybe it's the rest of the code related to moving hitobjects around that needs greater unification instead.

So I implemented selection blueprint layout logic without DHO <https://github.com/ppy/osu/commit/a353788b2f345588c0474956c64bf6d27b7b7835> (using #13449).
But then I realized `HitObjectComposer` is not available in tests so I cannot use `ScrollingHitObjectContainer` methods.
I'm not sure but I can factor out scrolling layout methods (`TimeAtPosition` and `PositionAtTime`) to a separate class. It should be also useful for non-DHO scrolling containers.

Yeah I don't know about doing that just for tests, may be worth just changing the tests. Long shot as I don't have all the context available but maybe `IPositionSnapProvider` can be leveraged somehow? Even if by implementing a mock or something.

review_comments: What's the null fallback here for? `blueprints` can't possibly be null, can it?
It is null when used during the base constructors.

I would hope nobody is reading this fallback value, given that it may cause children to be added to a different container than expected, but that said other test scenes seem to be doing similar things so...
Not sure why these are trimmed, but it seems like these were the only actual usages of this property. So it may be a good idea to remove them if they're no longer needed for some reason.
It was unrelated to the changes of this PR, but the lifetime logic is no longer unnecessary (and conflicting) because `DrawableHitObject` has its own logic for that. I removed the lifetime logic.
